courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: RequiredYear1PPD supports academic writing, research literacy, reflective goals and civic collaboration.

availableEvidence.description2: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
availableEvidence.profile: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
availableEvidence.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI
availableEvidence.methods: Scholarly literature searching and source evaluation; Literature synthesis; CARS model for research introductions; Reflective development planning; Community project co-design

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contribution: Empirical design, measurement, sampling, surveys/experiments and an actual team data-collection/analysis project give concrete tools for social and educational inquiry. No guaranteed educational dataset or teacher training is claimed.

availableEvidence.description2: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.
availableEvidence.profile: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
availableEvidence.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection
availableEvidence.methods: Survey design; Probability and nonprobability sampling; Experimental and nonexperimental research design; R and R Commander data analysis; Descriptive statistics and visualization; Scale-reliability analysis; One- and two-sample mean tests; ANOVA; Chi-square tests; Correlation and regression; Empirical data collection and analysis

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.contribution: Uses ethics and psychology to examine AI, including privacy, fairness, responsibility and human interaction.

availableEvidence.description2: Explores philosophical foundations and implications of AI. Examines the history of AI, ethical issues like interpretability, bias and alignment, debates about AI consciousness and implications for human nature.
availableEvidence.profile: Examines AI through ethical theory and psychological accounts of human behaviour and interaction. Ethical debates address fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Psychological perspectives consider development, clinical care, social and organizational relationships, forensic applications and cognitive neuroscience. Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.

availableEvidence.methods: Ethical-framework application; Philosophical argument evaluation; Psychological-literature synthesis; Theory-based analysis of AI applications; Research podcast scripting, recording and editing

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.contribution: Models and queries structured data using relational design and SQL.

availableEvidence.description2: Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science

availableEvidence.description2: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

availableEvidence.methods: R programming; ggplot visualization and grammar of graphics; Data cleaning, tidying and transformation; Data import and joins; Web scraping; Text-data analysis; Geospatial-data analysis

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.contribution: Develops and evaluates regression, classification and other predictive learning models.

availableEvidence.description2: Covers core machine learning techniques from linear regression to advanced tree‑based methods. Discusses strengths and weaknesses and applies methods to real data from fields like medicine, physics and economics.
availableEvidence.profile: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.

courses.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision

availableEvidence.description2: Covers processing and analysis of image data, including feature detection and tracking. Discusses applications in medicine, self‑driving vehicles, gaming, robotics and traffic management.

Spatial and spectral representations, colour and image statistics support filtering, segmentation, curve and feature detection, tracking and object classification. courses.name: Modern History
courses.contribution: Investigates political, economic and cultural modernity from 1815 through industrialisation, nationhood and ideological change.

availableEvidence.description2: Provides a chronological overview of history from 1815 to the present. Historical research and essays connect specific questions to evidence. A group project analyzes historical visions of the future as products of their own contexts and compares them with subsequent developments.

availableEvidence.description2: Guides students through the full arc of historical inquiry, from formulating research questions to engaging critically with sources. Emphasises methodological rigour and interdisciplinary thinking and culminates in a substantial research paper.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contribution: Uses competing theories and philosophical argument to evaluate ethical questions.

availableEvidence.description2: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

availableEvidence.profile: Surveys political thought from classical antiquity to contemporary debates, including European and non-European thinkers. courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.contribution: Language neurobiology, production/comprehension, acquisition, bilingualism, semantics, aphasia/dyslexia and hands-on experimental approaches give substantive language-processing inquiry. This supports language/communication questions within the digital option, without supplying digital-platform analysis or educational didactics.

availableEvidence.description2: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.contribution: Introduces cognitive and neuroscientific accounts of learning and behaviour and prepares students for later psychology courses.

availableEvidence.description2: Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods

With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.

Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.

candidates.label: Digital culture, platforms and AI society

stopping.assessment: Three provisional responses remain supported: culture/heritage and public interpretation; media critique with actual digital data/image methods and AI ethics; and language/learning with rhetorical education, development, youth prevention and social inquiry. They are coherent and substantively distinct as well as exceeding the pairwise30EC floor. Related coursework and bounded school/community projects do not replicate Tilburg’s Culture internship, complete pedagogy sequence or thesis. External cohort entry remains unresolved, so these are internal prototypes and no final comparison approval follows.

comparisonAlignment: Both study the cultural meaning of heritage. UCR focuses on African visual traditions and questions about their interpretation and display.
Both study the role of museums. UCR focuses on how museums and exhibitions shape the display and reception of modern art.
Both study transformations in modern Europe. UCR starts in 1815 and uses a wider historical and geographical frame.
Both examine how media technologies shape culture. UCR approaches digital networks through the history of earlier media.
Both examine popular media and social life. UCR uses examples from American television, film and digital media.
Both examine media and power. UCR focuses on race and representation in American cultural history.
Both explore changing ideas about human relationships with nature. UCR studies how media shape those ideas.
Both address public spheres. UCR situates them within contemporary theories of civil society and social movements.
Both develop qualitative inquiry. UCR covers qualitative research design, collection and analysis across a wider range of social research.
Both study persuasive communication. UCR draws on classical rhetoric and applies it through analysis and practice.
findings: All45selected course contributions read against current descriptions/profiles/topics/methods. Description-onlyDatabaseManagementSystems, AmericanCenturyResearch, SocialMovementsEnvironmentalJustice, Psycholinguistics, ClimateCommunication, RenaissanceItalyGlobalMediterranean, WritingArtsHistories and LiteraryMeaning receive full consideration for what their descriptions support. No missing profile is a rejection criterion. Eightcontribution scopes refined without rescheduling/replacing courses.

Closest Culture option materially engages exacttarget core through art/heritage/restitution, museums/curating, historical analysis, literature/myth/memory, moving images and humanities research. It is broader in Englishlanguage art/literature and does not recreate the cultural placement, education component sequence or a mandatorythesis.

Digitaloption has criticalmedia archaeology/representation/race/environment, publiccivil-society inquiry and substantive Rdata, SQLdatabase, Python/OpenCVimageprocessing, machinelearning andAIethics. Psycholinguistics supplies actual neurobiological/experimental language insight as a complement; not digitalplatform research by itself. Technical tools complement criticalmedia rather than claim a specialistAIengineering degree.

Educationoption integrates actual rhetorical primaryschoolcoaching, stylistics/literature, lifespan development, socialinfluence and substantive youthresilience/teacherresource design, backed by empiricalstatistics and socialtheory/inequality. This is bounded educational inquiry and communication practice, not a full didactics/teacherqualification path. No qualification absence is used to reject a candidate.

Three coherent programme identities and differing methods/progression satisfy qualitative distinctness and97.5/82.5/112.5ECpairwise differences. All three retain24unique7.5ECcourses/180EC,6terms of4,Year1PPD and at least6advanced; formal prerequisites and fixedcurrentXofferings rechecked mechanically.
